title: Kenyan Goat Bone Soup
community: Beloved across all communities — a butchery staple and home remedy
author: Mama Wanjiru

relatedDish.note: Goat Bone Soup (KEN056) and Beef Bone Soup (KEN050) use the same technique. Goat supu has a more intense, slightly gamier flavour — many Kenyans consider it the superior version. Both are sold at Kenyan butcheries as the ultimate warming restorative.

desc: Supu ya Mbuzi — Kenyan Goat Bone Soup — goat bones simmered for hours until the broth is golden, rich, and intensely flavourful. Considered by many Kenyans to be even more restorative than beef supu. The legendary butchery cure-all.
longDesc: At any Kenyan butchery that handles goat, there is almost always a pot of supu ya mbuzi on the fire — the intense, deeply savoury broth made from simmering goat bones for hours. Goat bones yield a particularly rich, fragrant broth that beef bones cannot quite match. Served with the marrow bones and a chapati for dipping, it is one of the most warming, restorative meals in Kenyan culinary tradition.
ingredients: 1.5 kg goat bones — knuckle, neck, and marrow bones
steps: Wash bones thoroughly. Place in a large pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil for 5 minutes, then discard this water.
Add 2.5 litres fresh cold water. Add all remaining ingredients except coriander and lemon.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to the lowest simmer. Cook partially covered for 2.5—3 hours.
Skim foam from the surface regularly for the first hour.
Season with salt in the final 30 minutes.
Serve hot with coriander, lemon juice, and chapati for dipping.
chefTips: The first boil-and-discard is essential for a clean, clear broth.
Goat supu should simmer gently — never boil hard.
Roasting the bones for 20 minutes at 200°C before simmering deepens the colour and flavour significantly.
commonMistakes: Boiling too vigorously — makes the broth cloudy.

faqs.q: Why is goat supu considered better than beef supu?
faqs.a: Goat bones tend to yield a more intensely flavoured, slightly more complex broth than beef — the higher myoglobin content gives it a deeper colour and richer taste. It is very much a matter of personal preference.

cookingScience: Goat bones are smaller and denser than beef bones, with a higher ratio of cartilage to total mass. This means goat supu extracts relatively more gelatin per kilogram of bones than beef supu, producing a broth with excellent body.
sustainabilityTips: Using bones reduces waste from the entire animal.
Freeze broth for use as stock throughout the week.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze for up to 3 months.
healthBenefits: Rich in gelatin and collagen supporting gut and joint health.
High in minerals from the bones.
culturalNote: Goat bone soup holds a special place in Kenyan culinary culture — it is the restorative served to those recovering from illness, the warming welcome for a guest on a cold evening, and the start of every great butchery meal.
regionalVariations: Spiced supu — with extra ginger and pepper.
Coastal supu — with a hint of coconut.
